matches.description: Watch Viktoria Plzeň vs Crvena zvezda highlights and goals from UEFA Europa League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on August 27, 2026. On August 27, 2026, the UEFA Europa League delivered a high-octane clash as Viktoria Plzeň hosted Crvena zvezda . Both teams entered the pitch with clear attacking intent, setting the stage for a match defined by dramatic shifts in momentum and clinical finishing. Early Goals Set the Tone The match ignited early when Viktoria Plzeň broke the deadlock in the 8th minute. Cheick Souare provided a pinpoint assist for Prince Adu , who clinicaly found the back of the net. The lead was short-lived, however, as Crvena zvezda struck back almost immediately. In the 11th minute, Mirko Ivanic leveled the score, ensuring the first half remained a tightly contested affair between two balanced sides. Red Card and a Shift in Power The second half proved to be the game's true turning point. In the 51st minute, Viktoria Plzeň had a golden opportunity to reclaim the lead, but Prince Adu missed his penalty. The drama intensified just two minutes later when Osman Bukari was shown a straight red card. Despite heavy protests from his teammates, the dismissal left Crvena zvezda to navigate the remainder of the match with only ten men. Capitalizing on the man advantage, Viktoria Plzeň surged forward. Denis Visinsky converted a penalty in the 58th minute to make it 2-1, and Patrik Hrosovsky quickly followed up in the 63rd minute with a goal assisted by Lukas Cerv . The tide had firmly turned in favor of the home side. Late Drama and Extra Time Mastery As the clock ticked toward full-time, the intensity reached a fever pitch. In the 90+5 minute, Christophe Kabongo extended the lead further from the penalty spot. The match then proceeded into extra time, which saw a flurry of yellow cards for Derrick Luckassen , Tomas Ladra , Vasilije Kostov , and Rade Krunic as tempers flared. In the 96th minute, David Krcik added gloss to the scoreline, finishing a move started by Kabongo . Despite the exhausting 120 minutes of play, Viktoria Plzeň remained disciplined to secure a resounding victory, while Crvena zvezda was left to rue the disciplinary lapse that changed the course of their European night.
